options: A function that returns a result set, rather than a single value
A function that can only be used inside WHERE
A synonym for a stored procedure
A function that always returns exactly one row
questions.explain: TVFs return rows, like a table would — which is why they can be joined to.

questions.q: Why can't a regular JOIN ... ON call a function using each row's own value?
options: ON is evaluated as a set-based condition, not row by row, so it can't reference 'the current row's value' while calling a function
Functions cannot be called anywhere inside a SELECT statement
JOIN...ON only works with two tables that have no functions involved at all
It actually can — CROSS APPLY does nothing a regular JOIN couldn't already do
questions.explain: This is precisely the gap CROSS APPLY fills — passing each row's own value into a function call.

questions.q: What does CROSS APPLY do differently from a regular JOIN?
options: The right side (a function call) is re-evaluated fresh for each left-side row, using that row's own values as input
It joins two static tables exactly like INNER JOIN, with no functional difference
It can only be used with system functions, never user-defined ones
It ignores the left table's rows entirely
questions.explain: This per-row re-evaluation is what makes CROSS APPLY different from an ordinary table-to-table JOIN.

questions.q: What happens to a row when CROSS APPLY's function returns nothing for it?
options: That row is dropped from the result, the same way INNER JOIN drops unmatched rows
The row is kept with NULLs filled in, like LEFT JOIN
The query fails with an error
The function is called again with a default value
questions.explain: CROSS APPLY behaves like INNER JOIN in this respect — OUTER APPLY (next lesson) is the LEFT JOIN equivalent.

questions.q: In 'CROSS APPLY dbo.ufnGetContactInformation(p.BusinessEntityID) AS ci', what does p.BusinessEntityID represent?
options: The current row's value from Person.Person, passed as input to the function for that specific row
A fixed constant value used for every row
The output alias for the function's result
A column that doesn't actually exist in AdventureWorks2012
questions.explain: This is the whole point of CROSS APPLY — each row of Person.Person supplies its own BusinessEntityID as the function's argument.
